title: TS SDK stream harmonizer: dual-surface interop, examples, and graceful degradation policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Build a small 'harmonizer' layer in the TypeScript SDK that exposes a single canonical streaming producer which can be consumed as either an AsyncIterator (for Node/ts-first ergonomics) or a Web ReadableStream (for web/Fetch-compatible consumers). Provide concrete examples, tests, and a degradation policy when only one primitive is available at runtime.
acceptance_criteria: A reusable helper (createStreamHarmonizer) that returns an object with both asyncIterator and readableStream accessors
Engineers can consume streamed responses using for-await-of and via pipeTo/pipes in browser without duplicate downloads or data races
Cancellation propagation works from both surfaces (calling return() on iterator or cancel() on ReadableStream triggers upstream abort)
Backpressure works in Node via async iterator pull semantics and in browser via underlying ReadableStream backpressure signals
E2E tests covering resume-after-network-interruption and retry-with-idempotency-token while streaming
Examples added to the SDK docs + a minimal sample repo demonstrating dual-consume patterns
steps: Design surface: single producer, twin accessors; no cloning of payload bytes unless consumer explicitly requests tee()
Implement core: an async generator that yields framed chunks and exposes a getReadableStream wrapper using a TransformStream/ReadableStream where available
Cancellation binding: wire AbortController; ensure both call sites share same controller and clean up KV cache references
Backpressure tuning: implement chunk coalescing threshold and maxBufferedChunks config; default conservative values to prioritize latency
Retries: define idempotency and retry-window tags; implement local buffering window to allow safe retry without duplicating previously sent content
Docs + samples: Write two examples (Node: for-await-of consumer with error-resume; Browser: fetch + response.body.getReader() and stream.pipeTo) and add to docs site
Test matrix: Node 18/20, Deno, Chrome/Firefox/Edge; simulated mid-stream disconnect, resume with restart-at-offset policy
notes: Background: many teams want async iterators in Node code and Web Streams for browser integrations; previous ad-hoc shims caused double-reads and subtle cancellation bugs
Trade-offs: holding a small buffer for potential retries increases memory but enables transparent retry without developer byte offsets; we expose config to tune this
Decision: expose async iterator as primary ergonomic surface (default in TS SDK) and export a helper getReadableStream() for web consumers to avoid API surface explosion
Alternative considered: create two independent producers (one for iterator, one for stream). Rejected due to duplicate network requests and cache complexity

Edge cases: consumers that call both iterator.next() and stream.getReader().read() concurrently are explicitly documented as unsupported; we provide a tee()-like utility that clones frames at consumer cost
Security: streaming responses may include sensitive partial tokens in trace logs; default SDK logging redacts chunks unless debug-mode is enabled
